blocks.body: A dependent is the main reason to own term life insurance; the common heuristic is 10–12 times the primary earner's income, and the DIME method gives a more specific number. A will is where you name a guardian for a minor child; without one, a court decides. Update beneficiary designations at the same time, and do not name a minor child directly: money left to a minor can end up with a court-appointed guardian, so name a trust or a custodian under your state's transfers-to-minors law.
blocks.plain: A child who depends on you is the main reason to have term life insurance. A common rule of thumb is 10–12 times the main earner's income; the DIME method gives a number that fits your household. A will is where you name a guardian for a young child — without one, a court chooses. Update the beneficiaries on your accounts at the same time. Don't name a young child as a beneficiary directly: a court may have to appoint someone to hold the money. Name a trust, or a custodian under your state's law for gifts to minors, instead.

draft.title: Plan the leave and the pay gap
draft.body: The drop in pay during leave is often the first money event. The federal FMLA gives eligible employees up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period for a birth or adoption, but the leave may be unpaid, and it asks for 30 days' notice when the date is foreseeable. Pay during leave may come from employer leave, short-term disability or a state paid-leave program if your state has one; check each one's claim rules before the due date.
draft.plain: Your pay may drop while you are on leave, and that is often the first money problem. The federal FMLA lets eligible workers take up to 12 workweeks of leave in a 12-month period for a birth or adoption and keep their job, but that leave can be unpaid. It asks you to tell your employer 30 days ahead when you know the date. Pay during leave can come from your employer's leave, short-term disability, or your state's paid-leave program if it has one. Check how to claim each one before the due date.
props: Pay drop during leave is often the first money event
FMLA: up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period for birth or adoption, for eligible employees
Pay sources: employer leave, short-term disability, state paid leave where it exists

draft.body: For 2026 the adoption credit covers qualified adoption expenses up to {{fig:adoption_credit_max}} per child, and up to {{fig:adoption_credit_refundable_max}} of it is refundable. If your employer has an adoption assistance program, those payments can also be excluded from income, but the same expenses cannot count for both. If a state has determined the child has special needs, the full credit can be claimed even with few or no expenses. The credit phases out at higher incomes.
draft.plain: For 2026 the adoption credit can cover adoption costs up to {{fig:adoption_credit_max}} per child, and up to {{fig:adoption_credit_refundable_max}} of it can come back as a refund. If your employer helps pay for adoption, that help can also be left out of your taxable income, but you can't use the same costs for both. If a state says the child has special needs, you can claim the full credit even if you had few or no adoption costs. The credit gets smaller at higher incomes.
